w10_T4_005168: Ines keeps 173 rolls of wallpaper in her decorating store, and she quotes every length in centimetres rather than in metres. A builder bought 51 rolls from her in one order. Each roll still in the store covers 6 wall panels in the flats she is fitting out. Her partner Grigor, whose own stock was much smaller than hers, contributed 53 panels of ready-cut board to the job. The hotel contract used up 240 panels, and the school corridor took another 211. How many panels were left for the rest of the work?
w10_T4_005175: The juice bar started the day with 172 oranges in its crate. Each orange was cut into 3 wedges for the press, so the count of pieces tripled. A member of staff found 3 wedges left over from the day before and put them with the rest. The bar has 14 stools along its counter. The morning rush used 106 wedges, and the afternoon got through 390 more. A late delivery was cut up to give 34 extra wedges. How many wedges did the bar have at the end?
w10_T4_005180: Kofi began the mosaic project with 79 ceramic tiles. His sister Amara, whose box held more than his, gave him 70 tiles from her own supply. Every tile was then scored and snapped into 4 small squares. Amara handed over 59 loose squares she had already cut, and Kofi found 52 more squares in a tin under the bench. The competition itself ran for 6 hours. Each square placed in the mosaic is worth 9 points from the judges. How many points was Kofi's mosaic worth?
w10_T4_005181: The allotment shed held 193 onion sets at the start of the planting weekend. Jonas planted 99 of them in the long bed by the fence. He put another 51 into the raised bed near the shed. Frost got into the shed and spoiled 30 of the sets that were still there. His neighbour Rita, who had bought far more than Jonas, gave him 72 sets from her own tray. Every set that went into the ground produced 2 onions at harvest. How many onions were harvested from those sets?
w10_T4_005187: The hospital shop had 98 newspapers on its stand when it opened in the morning. The delivery driver brought in 17 more before eight o'clock, and a second drop added 14. The ward upstairs has 30 beds. During the afternoon a wholesaler left 44 newspapers at the door, and in the early evening a dozen volunteers helped carry in 19 more from the van. Customers bought 61 newspapers over the course of the day. How many newspapers were left on the stand?
w10_T4_005198: The bottling line loaded 150 crates one shift, and every crate holds 6 bottles. A quality check released 44 further bottles from the holding bay into the same batch. Each bottle in the batch pours 6 servings at the tasting rooms. Every serving earns the company 9 loyalty points on the customer scheme. The points were divided equally among the 4 regional depots, and the manager followed only the share that went to the northern depot. That depot then split its points equally between its 2 shift teams. How many points did the northern depot's morning team receive?
w10_T4_005200: The building site took delivery of 236 boxes of nails in the morning, and each box contains 5 sealed packets. Every packet holds 4 nails of the long roofing type. The site employs 18 joiners across its two crews. During the afternoon the storeman found 69 loose nails in the bottom of a bin and added them to the tally. In the evening 65 nails came back unused from the roofing gang. How many nails did the site have?
w10_T4_005202: The leisure centre had 182 lockers standing empty when it opened in the morning. A cleaner cleared out 28 more that had been left locked overnight. Early swimmers took 31 of the free lockers before nine o'clock. At midday a school group filled 129 lockers in one noisy rush. In the evening 10 more lockers were taken by the badminton club. How many lockers were still empty at the end of the day?
w10_T4_005204: The school stockroom held 155 exercise books at the start of term, and it records lesson lengths in minutes rather than in hours. The office ordered 27 more, and a closing school nearby sent over 34. The caretaker shared all the books equally among the 4 classes in the year group, and the head of year then looked only at the set given to class 4B. Every book in that class was filled with 9 worksheets over the term. The teacher added 43 loose worksheets from her own folder. Each worksheet carries 8 questions. How many questions did class 4B work through?
w10_T4_005207: A dairy had 117 wheels of cheese maturing on its racks. It sold 55 of them to a wholesaler in the spring. A restaurant chain took another 26 wheels in the same month. Every wheel still on the racks was later cut into 7 wedges for the farm shop. The cheesemaker added 30 wedges from an older batch in the cold store and 25 wedges that had come back from a market stall. Each wedge is wrapped in 2 sheets of waxed paper before it goes on sale. How many sheets of waxed paper were needed?
w10_T4_005209: The warden counted 140 geese on the lake at first light. Another 47 dropped onto the water during the early morning, and 72 more came in from the fields before noon. Around midday 39 of the geese flew off towards the estuary. During the afternoon a further 50 geese landed on the far side of the lake. In the evening 47 more arrived as the light went. How many geese were on the lake at dusk?
w10_T4_005216: A stationery warehouse holds 113 cartons of notebooks, and every carton contains 6 notebooks. Half of the notebooks in stock are the lined kind. A returns pallet added 36 loose notebooks to the shelves. Each notebook in the warehouse is divided into 8 subject sections, and every section is made up of 6 printed pages. The binding room also has 77 loose printed pages waiting to be used. How many printed pages does the warehouse hold?
w10_T4_005219: Sanjay arrived at the arcade with 187 tokens, and the arcade sells its play in minutes rather than in hours. He used 90 tokens on the racing machines before lunch. He then handed 32 tokens to his friend Leila, who had arrived with none at all. Leila won a jackpot and gave Sanjay 80 tokens back. Every token he held was worth 6 minutes of play on the new simulator. The manager added 59 bonus minutes to his card for being the hundredth visitor. How many minutes of play did Sanjay have?
w10_T4_005226: The florist opened the morning with 168 stems in her buckets, and a dozen buckets stand along the back wall. A grower delivered 22 more stems before the shop got busy. Customers bought 62 stems during the morning. The florist then wired 4 silk leaves onto every stem that was still in the shop. During the afternoon 32 spare leaves arrived in a craft order, and in the evening a wholesaler sent 65 more. How many silk leaves did the florist have?
w10_T4_005232: Nora had 90 mosaic tiles saved for the community wall. Her colleague Ben, whose own store was larger, gave her 67 tiles from his workshop. Every tile in her tray breaks down into 9 coloured chips. The workshop also had 49 spare chips in a jar, which Nora added to the tray. The community wall swallowed 1288 chips over two weekends of work. Each chip that remained needs 6 dabs of glue to fix it to the next panel. How many dabs of glue will be needed?
w10_T4_005233: Hina spent the morning packing 146 gift boxes, and each box was filled with 7 scented candles. Every candle was then wrapped in 4 sheets of tissue paper before the lid went on. The drive to the northern shops takes 3 hours. During the afternoon the tissue-wrapped candles were shared equally among 4 delivery vans, and Hina's colleague Sam drove the van bound for Leeds. In the evening Sam was given 21 extra sheets of tissue for repacking on the road. How many sheets of tissue paper were in Sam's van?
w10_T4_005236: A mail-order company sent out 43 parcels of books in the first week, and 1 of them was lost by the carrier and written off. The following week it despatched 61 more parcels. The delivery van covers 90 kilometres on its round. Every parcel that arrived safely contained 5 books, and half of the titles were paperbacks. The warehouse then added 65 single books that had been ordered without a parcel. Each book on the invoice is priced at 8 dollars, and the invoice is written in dollars rather than in cents. What is the total price in dollars?
w10_T4_005239: The seed shop opened the morning with 123 seed trays on its outdoor bench. A landscaper arrived early and bought 115 of them for a park contract. Every tray still on the bench was found to hold 5 small pots. During the afternoon the owner counted 9 bulbs planted in each of those pots. She then added 67 loose bulbs from a sack in the shed. In the evening she calculated that every bulb would open 3 flowers next spring. How many flowers should the bulbs produce?
w10_T4_005242: A hardware shop had 178 padlocks hanging on its display wall, and it sells chain by the centimetre rather than by the metre. Customers bought 21 padlocks in the first week of the sale. A wholesaler then delivered 55 more. Over the second week 66 padlocks were sold to a storage firm. A late order brought in 73 further padlocks. Every padlock on the wall carries 9 loyalty stamps for the customer who buys it. How many loyalty stamps are on the display wall?
w10_T4_005243: Ola designed 76 posters for the museum campaign, and her colleague Tomas, who had made far fewer, gave her the 5 he had drawn. Every poster in the set was printed in 3 languages for the different districts. Each language version was then copied for all 8 branches of the museum service. Print sizes on the order are given in millimetres rather than in centimetres. Each branch copy has to be franked with 4 postage stamps to reach its site. How many postage stamps are needed?
w10_T4_005244: The bakery took 216 trays out of the proving room in the morning, and every tray carried 8 buns. Before ten o'clock 513 buns were sold over the counter. A café ordered 252 buns and collected them just before noon. The bakery has 4 ovens along the back wall. During the afternoon the bakers finished 62 more buns, and the second oven produced 26 further ones. In the evening 76 unsold buns came back from the market stall. How many buns were in the bakery at closing time?
w10_T4_005255: The fish farm lifted 49 nets in the morning, and each net filled 4 crates. The pier crew sent up 53 more crates from the boats. Every crate on the quay holds 9 fish. During the afternoon auction 1705 fish were sold to wholesalers. In the evening 403 fish were carried across to the smokehouse. How many fish were still on the quay?
w10_T4_005260: In the morning 4 lorries pulled into the grain yard, and each lorry carried 234 sacks. Half of the lorries in the fleet are less than a year old. Before noon 894 sacks were delivered on to the mill down the road. During the afternoon every sack still in the yard was split into 8 smaller bags for the retail trade. In the evening the storeman brought out 45 more bags that had been made up the previous week. How many bags were in the yard?
w10_T4_005261: Ruth was given 228 stickers for her holiday project. She shared them equally among 4 scrapbooks and then worked on the blue scrapbook alone. Half of the stickers in that book turned out to be from the older range. She peeled off 47 stickers that were creased and threw them away. The stickers still in the blue book were spread equally over its 2 remaining pages, and she then worked only on the left-hand page. Every sticker on that page was outlined with 4 gold stars. How many gold stars did Ruth draw?
w10_T4_005262: The cricket club started the season with 201 practice balls in its store. Over the summer 47 balls were lost in the long grass beyond the boundary. Another 33 split at the seam and were binned. The ground has 3 practice nets behind the pavilion. A sponsor donated 59 balls in July, and the club bought 52 more in August. Every ball in the store counts for 7 points in the county equipment tally, and the club was awarded 22 further points for its raffle. How many points did the club have in the tally?
